question: The main function of the flight data recorder is to:

options.text: Send the aircraft's position to the operator
Preserve aircraft data to find the cause of an accident
Monitor the engines for the maintenance crew only, with no other use

explanation: The FDR records aircraft parameters for the whole flight so that the cause of an accident can be determined. Its data is also used for trend analysis and troubleshooting.

question: Besides accident investigation, the FDR data is used for:

options.text: Calculating the take-off speeds for the next flight

explanation: The recorded data is also used for trend analysis and troubleshooting. In smaller aircraft the FDR may be combined with the CVR.

question: A modern FDR records the last:
explanation: The FDR stores the last 10 or 25 hours of data on a digital device in a shock-resistant box.

question: The FDR is normally located:

options.text: In the flight deck overhead panel, beside the CVR control
In the nose, behind the radar
At the rear, under the fin, in a red box

explanation: The shock-resistant box is painted red (or orange) and sits at the rear of the aircraft, normally under the fin, where it is most likely to survive.

question: What is fitted to the front of the FDR to help find it after an accident at sea?

options.text: An emergency locator transmitter on 121.5 MHz

explanation: An underwater locating device on the front emits ultrasonic pulses when immersed. It is required for the recorder.

question: Which of these is a component of the FDR system?

options.text: A radio altimeter antenna and receiver
A data interface and acquisition unit

explanation: The FDR system has a recording system, a control unit on the overhead panel, an event control on the pedestal, and a data interface and acquisition unit (DIAU).

question: Data from the DIAU is also sent to the aeroplane condition monitoring system for:

options.text: Navigation and guidance along the route

explanation: The ACMS takes the DIAU data plus inputs from many systems for monitoring and trend analysis, downloadable by printer, ACARS or the ATSU.

question: With the GND CTL switch at AUTO, the CVR and DFDR are powered:

options.text: Only when the crew presses ON
On the ground with an engine running, and in flight
Only in flight, and only with all engines running

explanation: In AUTO they are energised on the ground with one engine running and in flight, with engines running or stopped. ON powers them at once and lights the ON light.

question: What does the EVENT button on the pedestal do?

options.text: Puts a bookmark on the recording
Starts the recorder on the ground
Sends the data to the operator

explanation: EVENT sets an event mark on the DFDR recording so that the event can be found quickly when the data is analysed.

question: On the ground, the FDR stops automatically:

options.text: When the parking brake is set
5 minutes after the last engine shutdown
At the moment the last engine has stopped turning

explanation: The FDR stops automatically 5 minutes after the final engine shutdown.

question: The mandatory FDR parameters depend on:

options.text: The airline's own choice of parameters
The age and size of the aircraft

explanation: The required parameters depend on the age and size of the aircraft and are set out in the operating rules.

question: Which of these is a main FDR parameter?
explanation: Main parameters include time, pitch and roll, airspeed, pressure altitude, heading, normal acceleration, thrust or power, thrust lever position, flap/slat and spoiler/speed brake selection.

question: Which of these is an additional, not a main, FDR parameter?
explanation: Additional parameters include primary flight control and trim positions, radio altitude, displayed navigation information, cockpit warnings and landing gear position.

question: The minimum FDR recording time for aeroplanes over 5700 kg is:
explanation: Aeroplanes over 5700 kg must record at least 25 hours, including all the main parameters.

question: Turbine aeroplanes under 5700 kg with more than 9 seats must record for at least:
explanation: For these lighter turbine aeroplanes the recording time may be no less than 10 hours.

question: Above which mass must the additional parameters also be recorded?
explanation: Aeroplanes over 27 000 kg maximum take-off mass must also record the additional parameters.

question: When must the FDR start recording?

options.text: At the start of the take-off roll on the runway
Before the aeroplane can move under its own power

explanation: It must start before the aeroplane can move under its own power, in practice at first engine start, and stop after it can no longer do so, 5 minutes after the last engine shutdown.

question: Which aeroplanes may combine the FDR with the CVR in one unit?

options.text: None; they must always be separate

explanation: Aeroplanes of 5700 kg or less may combine them. Above 5700 kg there must be two recorders: a separate FDR and CVR, or two combined recorders.

question: An aeroplane over 5700 kg has combined recorders. How many must it carry?
explanation: Above 5700 kg two recorders are needed, so with combined units two combined recorders must be fitted.

question: An aeroplane may be dispatched with an inoperative FDR for no more than:
explanation: Dispatch is possible if repair is not reasonably practicable, for no more than 8 further consecutive flights and 72 hours since the failure, and with any required CVR working.

question: For dispatch with an inoperative FDR, which other condition applies?

options.text: Any required CVR must work, unless combined with the FDR
The aeroplane must fly by day only
The flight must be under VFR
ATC must be told before each flight that it is inoperative

explanation: Any cockpit voice recorder required to be carried must be operative, unless it is combined with the failed FDR.
